summary: The owner's instruction: no ice caps or glaciers; Dia-thìr lies between Ireland and Scotland. Record 1: latitude and longitude put the island at about 54.6-56.0 N, 5.8 W; the climate settings give a mild oceanic island (sea-level annual mean 9-10 C, colder only with height). Record 11 is recomputed from them as Azgaar computes it. The 37 Glacier cells (record 16) become Moor on the windy coast of the far north-west (17) and Grassland at the northern end of the shire of Seann Vell of the west (20); their people (record 21) are thin like the moor round them (the mean of their moor neighbours). No icebergs (record 39) and the ice layer saved empty (record 5). The rural totals of the cultures and states follow the population array (derived in map_reconcile.py). The land layer's latitude, coordinates and state rural totals are set aside: the first two are replaced here, the last is derived.

map_edits.why: The island lies between Ireland and Scotland: with the map 2 degrees of latitude tall (mapSize 1.13, 0.2 miles to the unit), latitude 18.99 puts the top of the map at 56.2 N and the island's coasts between about 54.6 and 56.0 N.
And between Ireland and Scotland in longitude: the map spans 8.0 to 3.6 W, the island's middle near 5.8 W, the longitude of the North Channel.
Recomputed by Azgaar's own formula (Coordinates.calculate) from mapSize 1.13, latitude 18.99, longitude 51.63 and the 1536x702 canvas.

A mild oceanic island: with the equator at 27 C (Azgaar's default) and the north pole at -4 C, the sea-level annual mean is 9-10 C across the island's latitudes, as on the coasts of the North Channel.
See the equator: the pole value sets the slope of the sea-level temperature with latitude; -34 made the island subarctic.

The grid temperatures made anew from the settings above, as Azgaar makes them: 9 C at sea level, falling only with height (to about 2 C on the highest summit, some 3,500 ft); nowhere below freezing, nowhere near the -5 C at which Azgaar lays down glacier. The frame is given (the one set above), so the later place layer (place.json), which moves the island into the Atlantic, leaves the temperatures as they are.
